A Brazilian court has ordered Apple to tighten age controls on a casino-style app on the App Store, including requiring users to pass age verification before making in-app purchases. Here are the details.

Brazil orders Apple to strengthen App Store age checks

According to Tilt, a court in São Paulo has approved an emergency injunction requiring Apple to restrict minors' access to the "Casino Roulette: Roulettist" app.

In July of this year, four children's and adolescents' rights organisations filed a civil lawsuit alleging that minors were able to download casino-style games from the App Store and purchase virtual chips with real money, even though Casino Roulette: Roulettist is labelled as being for users aged 18 and above. The court subsequently issued the relevant ruling.

According to Tilt, the ruling gives Apple five days to block new downloads of Casino Roulette: Roulettist by users registered as minors, and requires "age verification when purchasing virtual chips with real money to continue playing or expand the in-app experience".

Beyond the specific app, the ruling also prohibits Apple from listing new apps with similar casino-style mechanics on the App Store without effective age control measures in place.

Tilt reports that the court also ordered Apple to preserve all records related to the app and submit a technical report detailing the measures taken. The court further stipulated that Apple would face a fine of 100,000 reais (approximately US$19,500) per day for non-compliance.

Tilt has reached out to Apple for comment on the matter, but had not received a response by the time of publication.
